summary: Rebbi teaches us to choose a good path, to be careful with every mitzvah, small or big, and to remember that Hashem sees and hears everything we do.

chunks.en: Rebbi says:

words.note: Rabbi Yehudah HaNasi, who put together the Mishnah.

chunks.he: אֵיזוֹהִי דֶרֶךְ יְשָׁרָה שֶׁיָּבֹר לוֹ הָאָדָם,
chunks.en: Which is the right path that a person should choose for himself?
Whatever brings honor to the one who does it

words.en: to the one who does it

chunks.en: and brings him honor from other people.
And be as careful with a light mitzvah as with a heavy one,
because you do not know the reward
for each of the mitzvos.

chunks.he: וֶהֱוֵי מְחַשֵּׁב הֶפְסֵד מִצְוָה כְּנֶגֶד שְׂכָרָהּ,
chunks.en: And weigh the loss of a mitzvah against its reward,
chunks.explain: What you give up for a mitzvah is small next to its reward.

chunks.en: and the gain of an aveirah against its loss.
Look at three things
and you will not come to sin:
Know what is above you:
an eye that sees and an ear that hears,
and all your deeds are written in a book.

summary: Rabban Gamliel teaches that Torah learning goes well together with working for a living, and that people who work for the community should do it for the sake of Heaven.

chunks.en: Rabban Gamliel, the son of
Rabbi Yehudah HaNasi, says:

words.note: The leader of the Jewish people.

chunks.he: יָפֶה תַלְמוּד תּוֹרָה עִם דֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ,
chunks.en: Torah learning is beautiful together with a way of earning a living,
because working hard at both makes a person forget sin.
And any Torah that has no work with it
will in the end stop, and it pulls along sin.
And all who work for the community
should work with them for the sake of Heaven,

chunks.he: שֶׁזְּכוּת אֲבוֹתָם מְסַיַּעְתָּן וְצִדְקָתָם עוֹמֶדֶת לָעַד.
chunks.en: because the merit of their fathers helps them, and their goodness lasts forever.
And you, I will give you a lot of reward,
as if you had done it all yourselves.

summary: This mishnah warns us to be careful with rulers, because they are only friendly when it helps them, and they don't stand by a person when he is in trouble.

chunks.en: Be careful with the rulers,
because they only bring a person close
for their own needs.
They look like friends when it is good for them,

chunks.he: וְאֵין עוֹמְדִין לוֹ לָאָדָם בִּשְׁעַת דָּחְקוֹ:
chunks.en: but they do not stand by a person when he is in trouble.

summary: Rabban Gamliel teaches to do what Hashem wants as if it were what you want. Hillel teaches not to separate from the community, not to be too sure of yourself, not to judge others too fast, and not to push off learning until later.

chunks.en: He used to say:
Do His will as if it were your will,
so that He will do your will as if it were His will.
Put aside your will because of His will,

chunks.he: כְּדֵי שֶׁיְּבַטֵּל רְצוֹן אֲחֵרִים מִפְּנֵי רְצוֹנֶךָ.
chunks.en: so that He will put aside what others want because of what you want.
Hillel says:
Do not separate yourself from the community,

chunks.he: וְאַל תַּאֲמִין בְּעַצְמְךָ עַד יוֹם מוֹתְךָ,
chunks.en: and do not trust yourself until the day you die,
chunks.explain: Even a good person can still go wrong.

chunks.en: and do not judge your friend
until you are in his place.

chunks.he: וְאַל תֹּאמַר דָּבָר שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לִשְׁמֹעַ,
chunks.en: And do not say something that cannot be understood,
saying it will be understood in the end.
And do not say: When I have free time I will learn,
because maybe you will not have free time.

summary: Hillel teaches what different kinds of people cannot do: someone with no learning can't fear sin properly, a shy person can't learn, and an impatient person can't teach. Where there is no one to lead, try to be the leader.

chunks.en: He used to say:
An empty person cannot fear sin,

words.note: Someone with no learning and no good ways.

chunks.en: and an unlearned person cannot be truly pious,

words.note: Am ha'aretz: someone who did not learn.

chunks.en: and a shy person cannot learn,
and an impatient person cannot teach,
and not everyone who does a lot of business becomes wise.
And in a place where there are no men,
try to be a man.
chunks.explain: Where no one is acting right, you be the one to act right.

summary: Hillel saw a skull floating on the water and taught that Hashem pays people back measure for measure.

chunks.en: He also saw one skull
that was floating on top of the water.
He said to it:
Because you drowned others,
they drowned you. And in the end, those who drowned you will be drowned.

summary: Hillel teaches that having more things can bring more trouble, but more Torah, learning, advice and tzedakah bring more good. A good name and Torah are things a person truly gets for himself.

chunks.en: He used to say:
One who adds flesh
adds worms.
chunks.explain: Eating too much just makes more for the worms in the grave.

chunks.en: One who adds possessions
adds worry.
One who adds wives
adds witchcraft.
One who adds maidservants
adds bad behavior.
One who adds servants
adds stealing.
One who adds Torah
adds life.
One who adds sitting and learning

words.note: Sitting and learning in the yeshivah.

chunks.en: adds wisdom.
One who adds advice
adds understanding.
One who adds tzedakah
adds peace.
One who gets a good name
gets it for himself.
One who gets words of Torah for himself
gets for himself life in the World to Come.

summary: Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai teaches not to take credit for learning a lot of Torah, because that is what we were made for. He praises each of his five great students.

chunks.en: Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai
received the Torah from Hillel and from Shammai.
He used to say:
If you learned a lot of Torah,
do not take the credit for yourself,
because that is what you were created for.
He had five students,
Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai,
and these are they:
Rabbi Eliezer ben Hurkenos,
and Rabbi Yehoshua ben Chananyah,
and Rabbi Yosi the Kohen,
and Rabbi Shimon ben Nesanel,
and Rabbi Elazar ben Arach.
He used to list their praises:
Rabbi Eliezer ben Hurkenos
is a sealed pit that does not lose a drop.
Rabbi Yehoshua ben Chananyah:
how fortunate is the mother who gave birth to him.

words.en: the one who gave birth to him

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosi the Kohen
is pious. Rabbi Shimon ben Nesanel

words.note: A chasid: someone who does even more than he must.

chunks.en: fears sin.
And Rabbi Elazar ben Arach
is a spring that keeps getting stronger.
chunks.explain: He keeps coming up with new ideas.

chunks.en: He used to say:
If all the Sages
of Israel were on one side of a scale,
and Eliezer ben Hurkenos on the other side,
he would outweigh them all.
Abba Shaul says in his name:
If all the Sages of Israel were

chunks.he: בְּכַף מֹאזְנַיִם וְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן הוֹרְקְנוֹס
chunks.en: on one side of a scale, and Rabbi Eliezer ben Hurkenos
was with them too,

chunks.he: וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲרָךְ בְּכַף שְׁנִיָּה,
chunks.en: and Rabbi Elazar ben Arach on the other side,
he would outweigh them all.

summary: Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai asked his students what is the best path for a person and what is the worst. He agreed most with Rabbi Elazar: a good heart, and the opposite, a bad heart.

chunks.en: He said to them:
Go out and see which is the good path
that a person should stick to.
Rabbi Eliezer says:
A good eye.
chunks.explain: Being happy for others and wishing them well.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehoshua says:
A good friend.
Rabbi Yosi says:
A good neighbor.
Rabbi Shimon says:
One who sees what will come.
chunks.explain: He thinks ahead about what will happen.

chunks.en: Rabbi Elazar says:
A good heart.
He said to them:
I like the words
of Elazar ben Arach more than your words,
because your words are included in his words.

chunks.he: אָמַר לָהֶם צְאוּ וּרְאוּ אֵיזוֹהִי דֶרֶךְ רָעָה
chunks.en: He said to them: Go out and see which is the bad path
that a person should keep away from.
Rabbi Eliezer says:
A bad eye.
Rabbi Yehoshua says:
A bad friend.
Rabbi Yosi says:
A bad neighbor.
Rabbi Shimon says:
One who borrows and does not pay back.
Borrowing from a person
is like borrowing from Hashem, blessed is He,
as it says (Tehillim 37): One who borrows,
a wicked one, does not pay back,
but a tzaddik is kind and gives.
chunks.explain: Hashem, the Tzaddik, pays back for him.

chunks.en: Rabbi Elazar says:
A bad heart.
He said to them:
I like the words
of Elazar ben Arach more than your words,
because your words are included in his words.

summary: Rabbi Eliezer teaches: care about your friend's honor like your own, don't get angry easily, do teshuvah every day, and stay close to the Sages but treat them with great respect.

chunks.en: They each said three things.
Rabbi Eliezer says:

chunks.he: יְהִי כְבוֹד חֲבֵרְךָ חָבִיב עָלֶיךָ כְּשֶׁלָּךְ,
chunks.en: Let your friend's honor be as dear to you as your own,
and do not get angry easily.
And do teshuvah one day before you die.
chunks.explain: Nobody knows when he will die, so do teshuvah every day.

chunks.he: וֶהֱוֵי מִתְחַמֵּם כְּנֶגֶד אוּרָן שֶׁל חֲכָמִים,
chunks.en: And warm yourself by the fire of the Sages,
but be careful with their coals so you don't get burned,
because their bite is the bite of a fox,
and their sting is the sting of a scorpion,
and their hiss is the hiss of a snake,
and all their words are like burning coals.

summary: Rabbi Yehoshua teaches that a bad eye, the yetzer hara, and hating people take a person out of the world.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehoshua says:
A bad eye,
and the yetzer hara,
and hating people,
take a person out of the world.

summary: Rabbi Yosi teaches: care about your friend's money like your own, work hard to learn Torah because you don't get it automatically, and do everything for the sake of Heaven.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosi says:

chunks.he: יְהִי מָמוֹן חֲבֵרְךָ חָבִיב עָלֶיךָ כְּשֶׁלָּךְ,
chunks.en: Let your friend's money be as dear to you as your own,
and get yourself ready to learn Torah,
because it is not an inheritance for you.
chunks.explain: You don't get it from your father; you must work for it.

chunks.en: And let all your deeds be for the sake of Heaven.

summary: Rabbi Shimon teaches to be careful with saying Shema and davening, to daven from the heart and ask Hashem for mercy, and not to think of yourself as wicked.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon says:
Be careful with saying Shema and with davening.
And when you daven,
do not make your tefillah a fixed habit,
chunks.explain: Don't just say the words like a chore.

chunks.en: but ask for mercy and beg before
Hashem, blessed is He,
as it says (Yoel 2): For He is kind
and merciful, slow to anger, and full of
kindness, and He changes His mind about bad things.
And do not be wicked in your own eyes.

summary: Rabbi Elazar teaches: learn Torah with energy, know how to answer someone who mocks the Torah, and remember that you work for Hashem, who will surely pay you.

chunks.en: Rabbi Elazar says:
Be busy and eager to learn Torah,
and know what to answer an apikores.

words.note: Someone who makes fun of the Torah.

chunks.en: And know before Whom you work.
And your Employer can be trusted
to pay you the reward for your work.

summary: Rabbi Tarfon compares life to a work day: the time is short, there is a lot to do, the reward is great, and the Master is pushing.

chunks.en: Rabbi Tarfon says:
The day is short and there is a lot of work,
and the workers are lazy,
and the pay is great,
and the Master of the house is pushing.

summary: Rabbi Tarfon teaches that you don't have to finish all the work, but you may not stop trying. Hashem will surely pay a great reward to those who learn, in the World to Come.

chunks.en: He used to say:
It is not your job to finish the work,

chunks.he: וְלֹא אַתָּה בֶן חוֹרִין לִבָּטֵל מִמֶּנָּה.
chunks.en: but you are not free to stop doing it.
If you learned a lot of Torah,
they give you a lot of reward.
And your Employer can be trusted
to pay you the reward for your work.
And know that the reward
of tzaddikim is in the time to come.
